title: Unify release manifests and publish hooks for Python/TS/Go SDKs
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary:
We need a single, deterministic release pipeline and artifact manifest format for the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDK packages. Current pipelines are inconsistent (different metadata fields, ad-hoc checksums, and divergent signing mechanisms). This task will implement:
- a shared release manifest (JSON) that accompanies every published bundle (wheel/sdist, npm tgz, go zip) containing: exact artifact filenames, semantic version, commit SHA, build timestamp (UTC), builder identity, list of files with SHA256 checksums, and a provenance statement URL/attestation reference.
- GitHub Actions publishing hooks that generate the manifest, upload artifacts to the appropriate registry (PyPI, npm, Go proxy), and publish an in-toto/SLSA-style attestation (signed provenance.json).
- Deterministic versioning guard rails: only allow release runs from tagged commits (vX.Y.Z) and include a post-release verification job that re-fetches artifacts and validates checksums and signatures.
- Release examples that demonstrate packaging streaming and retry integration tests as part of the release validation stage (packaged under examples/integration).

Goals:
- Single manifest format across languages to simplify downstream verification and our release notes automation.
- Cryptographic provenance (signed) for all published SDK artifacts to support customer verifiers and internal security reviews.
- CI-level deterministic gates so identical artifacts are produced for a given tag.
- Developer ergonomics: local helper script to build and sign artifacts for manual releases.

Non-goals:
- Replacing existing external registries or proxies.
- Full SLSA 3+ pipeline in first iteration; we target SLSA attestation generation and signature verification compatible with in-toto v1 statements.

Design (high level):
1) Manifest schema: manifest-v1.json with flat keys: version, tag, commit, build_time, builder, artifacts: list-of-objects-represented-as-strings (filename|sha256|size|type), provenance_url, channels (npm|pypi|go), notes_url. We will serialize artifacts as pipe-delimited strings in the manifest (to keep JSON flat) e.g. "wheel-0.12.3-py3-none-any.whl|abcd1234...|12345|wheel".
2) Signing: CI will sign the manifest and provenance JSON using an ephemeral signing key provisioned via GitHub Actions OIDC to a short-lived KMS key or by using GitHub's sigstore-compatible cosign with ephemeral identity. The signature and public verification info will be uploaded alongside the manifest.
3) CI Workflows: a reusable GH Action in .github/actions/publish that: builds artifacts (python: build wheel/sdist; ts: npm pack; go: GOSUMDB-compatible zip), computes checksums, creates manifest, runs attestations, signs artifacts, publishes to registries, then triggers a verification job on a separate runner to re-download and validate.
4) Local dev flow: scripts/release/prepare_release.sh and scripts/release/verify_release.sh that recreate the build locally for a tag. These scripts are documented and included in the README for maintainers.

Acceptance criteria:
- A tagged run (vX.Y.Z) produces: manifest-v1.json, manifest-v1.json.sig, provenance-v1.json, provenance-v1.json.sig, and published packages in the target registries.
- Post-publish verification job succeeds and checksums/signatures validate.
- Security team signs off on attestation format (POAM attached).
- Example integration tests for streaming and retry behavior are packaged and run as part of release verification.
- Documentation added to SDK root README describing how to verify artifact provenance locally.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit: manifest generation unit tests for all SDK build scripts (python, ts, go) to check checksum formatting and field presence.
- Integration: run release job against test registries (test.pypi, npm test scope, local go proxy) to validate end-to-end flow.
- Staging: run full flow in a staging org repository with ephemeral keys and manual review.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature branch PoC (this ticket) -> PR for action and scripts.
2) Run against test registries and get security review.
3) Flip a repo-level feature flag to enable in nightly releases for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual enable on production release workflows.

Migration notes for existing releases:
- Old artifacts that lack manifest will be grandfathered; we will not retroactively sign them.
- Add a compatibility flag for legacy clients that expect per-language metadata locations.

Open questions / risks:
- How to store/publicize the signing public key and rotation story? (we propose using cosign transparency logs + public key published in releases.redwood.inference/trusted-keys).
- Need to confirm if npm registry accepts externally signed manifests; otherwise we will store signatures in GitHub Releases.
- Go module verification: ensure dist packaging is compatible with go proxy checksum validation; may need to publish to GOPRIVATE for internal modules.

Work items (high level):
- Add manifest generator to python/ts/go build pipelines (ENG-33109.1)
- Create reusable GH Action publish hook and verification job (ENG-33109.2)
- Wire cosign/sigstore integration for ephemeral signing (ENG-33109.3)
- Documentation + local helper scripts (ENG-33109.4)
- Integration tests for streaming/retries packaged as release smoke tests (ENG-33109.5)

Links and artifacts:
- GitHub actions PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1542 (WIP)
- Draft manifest schema: https://docs.google.com/document/d/manifest-spec-placeholder
- Security review ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/SEC-1112
- Staging publish dashboard (internal): https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/staging-releases

Notes on developer ergonomics:
- The packaged integration example will live in examples/release-smoke/ and will include a small echo server used to test streaming ergonomics and retry backoff that matches production SDK behavior. This allows us to catch regressions in how streamed responses are packaged or retried across language SDKs.

Acceptance tests (detailed):
- Given a tag vA.B.C, CI builds artifacts, manifest contains exact filenames and checksums, cosign verifies signatures, and verification job re-downloads artifacts and validates checksums and verifies attestation signature.
- Examples release smoke test validates streaming chunk order and retry idempotency across all three SDKs.
